events.title: Next.js open sourced
events.summary: Vercel (then ZEIT) released Next.js — a React framework for server-rendered universal JavaScript apps.
events.about: Next.js wraps React with file-based routing, server rendering, and static generation — one codebase for SEO-friendly pages and interactive UI. Used for marketing sites, docs, e-commerce storefronts, and full-stack apps on Vercel. Example: a blog that pre-renders HTML at build time but hydrates React on the client.

narrative.whyChosen: Next.js became the default way to ship React with SSR, routing, and static generation in one toolchain.
narrative.whyImportant: It bridged SPA ergonomics with SEO-friendly server rendering before React Server Components.
narrative.problemSolved: React alone did not solve routing, data loading, or SSR — every team rebuilt the same webpack stack.

events.title: Yarn released
events.summary: Facebook, Google, Exponent, and Tilde released Yarn 0.1.0 on October 11, 2016 — a fast, deterministic npm-compatible package manager.
events.about: Yarn introduced lockfiles (`yarn.lock`), parallel installs, and checksum verification when npm still struggled with reproducible builds. Teams switched overnight for faster CI and consistent `node_modules` trees. Yarn 2+ later pushed Plug'n'Play; npm caught up with `package-lock.json` — but Yarn forced the ecosystem to treat dependency resolution as infrastructure, not an afterthought.

narrative.whyChosen: Yarn addressed npm's speed and determinism gaps with a drop-in alternative backed by major platforms.
narrative.whyImportant: It popularized lockfiles and pushed npm to improve — raising the bar for JavaScript supply-chain hygiene.
narrative.problemSolved: JavaScript projects needed reproducible installs and faster CI when npm's client was slow and non-deterministic.

events.title: Audrey Tang appointed Taiwan digital minister
events.summary: Audrey Tang was appointed minister without portfolio for digital affairs in Taiwan on October 1, 2016 — the youngest and first transgender cabinet minister.
events.about: Tang promoted radical government transparency, open data, and participatory budgeting — exporting Taiwan's civic tech model during COVID contact tracing and beyond.

narrative.whyChosen: Tang brought open-source values into national government at cabinet level.
narrative.whyImportant: It demonstrated hackers could reform public institutions from inside government.
narrative.problemSolved: Governments lacked technical leadership that understood open collaboration.
